# zurg

> zurg is a Go daemon that presents a debrid account or a directory of NZBs as a virtual filesystem. Six debrid services are supported and so is Usenet. It stores no media and it accepts no uploads.

- [zurg](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/index.md): zurg
- [Setup](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/setup/index.md): The binary installer is the shortest path on Linux, macOS and Windows. Docker remains available when a container fits the host better.
- [Providers](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/providers/index.md): A provider is one account zurg builds its library from. Every account is one entry under providers: in config.yml. Run one account or run six. A release held by more than one of them is listed once and read from whichever account can serve it at the time.
- [Guides](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/guides/index.md): Working with the library: Usenet, the arrs, __magic__, and media servers.
- [Migrating to zurg](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/migrate/index.md): Read this page first. It applies to every migration and it is most of what you need. The per-server pages are short because this one carries the shared part.
- [Reference](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/reference/index.md): Look-up pages. Nothing here is a walkthrough. Read them when you know what you want and need the exact name of it.
- [Internals](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/internals/index.md): How zurg is built. What it was measured at. The design notes behind the awkward parts. Written for someone about to change the code. Nothing here is needed to run zurg.

## Setup

- [Linux binary setup](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/setup/linux.md): The optional sponsor bootstrap installs the supported system packages, downloads the matching CPU build and runs setup plus diagnostics:
- [Docker setup](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/setup/docker.md): This guide runs zurg in Docker while making its FUSE mount visible on the Linux host. Docker supplies zurg, rclone and ffprobe and keeps the container running.
- [macOS Tutorial](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/setup/macos.md): The optional sponsor bootstrap installs macFUSE when needed, downloads the correct Intel or Apple silicon build and runs the provider chooser and
- [Windows, the binary, from scratch](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/setup/windows.md): Run the optional sponsor bootstrap from PowerShell. It installs WinFsp through UAC, downloads zurg and runs the provider chooser and diagnostics:

## Providers

- [Real-Debrid](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/providers/realdebrid.md): type: realdebrid
- [TorBox](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/providers/torbox.md): type: torbox
- [AllDebrid](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/providers/alldebrid.md): type: alldebrid
- [Premiumize](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/providers/premiumize.md): type: premiumize
- [Debrid-Link](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/providers/debridlink.md): type: debridlink
- [Offcloud](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/providers/offcloud.md): type: offcloud
- [Usenet](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/providers/usenet.md): type: nzb
- [TorBox limits and how zurg adapts to them](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/providers/torbox-limits.md): Zurg's library behaviour grew around Real-Debrid's constraints. TorBox's are different in kind, not just in magnitude, and driving it like Real-Debrid gets the account rate-limited within seconds of a first library scan.
- [TorBox news server](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/providers/torbox-news-server.md): A TorBox Pro subscription bundles a Usenet account. It is a real NNTP server and zurg can use it as an ordinary type: nzb provider. This page records what that server is and what it is worth as a provider slot.
- [ElfHosted news server](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/providers/elfhosted-news-server.md): ElfHosted bundles a Usenet account with its Stremio addon plans and calls it Usenet Essential. This page records what that server is. Everything below was measured on 2026-09-04 from one host.

## Guides

- [Usenet with zurg](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/guides/usenet.md): zurg's nzb backend turns a directory of .nzb files into a mounted library. There is no downloader, no completed folder, and nothing on disk but the NZB
- [Sonarr and Radarr, step by step](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/guides/sonarr-radarr.md): Point Sonarr and Radarr at zurg and they grab from Usenet without a Usenet client — no download, no unpack, no disk. Every step below, with the screen you should be looking at.
- [Sonarr and Radarr with torrents, step by step](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/guides/sonarr-radarr-torrents.md): The previous walkthrough pointed the *arrs at zurg for Usenet, with zurg answering as a SABnzbd. This is the other half: zurg answers as a qBittorrent, the *arrs hand it a magnet or a .torrent instead of an NZB, and the release goes onto a debrid account instead of a news server.
- [__magic__, a directory you can organise](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/guides/magic.md): Every other directory zurg serves is computed. movies holds what matches the movies filter, __all__ holds everything, and a release's folder holds the files its account says it has — so the layout is a view of the library, recomputed on every refresh, and there is nowhere to put anything.
- [Renaming releases and files](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/guides/renaming.md): zurg's mount is writable in exactly one way: you can rename a release folder or a file inside one, anywhere in the library. It is on by default. Nothing is
- [Plex Features & Capabilities](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/guides/plex.md): Config keys documented in config.md/config.example.yml: plex_server_url, plex_token, plex_match_every_mins (default 1440), plex_watchlist_enabled, plex_watchlist_check_every_secs (default 5s), mount_path (required for matching/scan path building).
- [Acquisition sources](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/guides/acquisition.md): Plex watchlist and Seerr feed the same durable engine. Adapters discover requests and resolve media IDs. The engine owns progress, retries and acknowledgement.
- [Plex watchlist acquisition](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/guides/plex-watchlist.md): Plex watchlist is an adapter on the shared acquisition engine, alongside Seerr. Existing watchlist.enabled and legacy Plex watchlist settings keep working. The adapter resolves cloud-watchlist titles and uses the shared Newznab executor to save NZBs.
- [The Stremio addon](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/guides/stremio.md): zurg can answer Stremio as an addon: the client asks for streams by IMDb id, zurg searches your Newznab indexers, and picking a stream pulls that release's NZB into the Usenet backend and plays it — the search-per-play model streamnzb had, on top of zurg's library, repair and archive streaming.
- [Jellyfin Features & Capabilities](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/guides/jellyfin.md): Config keys (config.md, config.example.yml): jellyfin_server_url (string, default ), jellyfin_token (string, default ). Both ship commented out in config.example.yml and are absent from config.simple.yml.
- [Local debrid libraries and portable zurgtorrents](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/guides/local-libraries.md): A local library takes its membership from portable .zurgtorrent files. It appears in the normal WebDAV, HTTP and provider directories. Importing files, listing them and refreshing the catalog do not add torrents or resolve download links.
- [zurg for Android and Google TV](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/guides/android.md): The Android app runs its bundled zurg engine on the device. One app adapts to phones, tablets, Android TV and Google TV. Android 8.0 or newer is required. Fire TV can sideload the same APK; use a WebDAV player when no system Files app is installed.

## Migrating

- [Migrating from AltMount to zurg](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/migrate/altmount.md): Read the shared page first. The trash guard lives there. So does the reason your library lands in __magic__ rather than in a symlink farm.
- [Migrating from decypharr to zurg](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/migrate/decypharr.md): Read the shared page first. The trash guard lives there. So does the reason your library lands in __magic__ rather than in a symlink farm.
- [Migrating from InfiniDysk to zurg](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/migrate/infinidysk.md): Read the shared page first. The trash guard lives there. So does the reason your library lands in __magic__ rather than in a symlink farm.
- [Migrating from nzbdav to zurg](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/migrate/nzbdav.md): Read the shared page first. The trash guard lives there. So does the reason your library lands in __magic__ rather than in a symlink farm.
- [Migrating from streamnzb v5.1.0 to zurg](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/migrate/streamnzb.md): Be clear about what this migration is before starting it. It is a change of model rather than a cutover. streamnzb has no filesystem and no WebDAV and no mount and no Plex library.

## Reference

- [zurg Configuration Documentation](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/reference/config.md): This document details all available configuration options for zurg. Configure these options in your config.yml file.
- [Command line](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/reference/cli.md): The zurg binary is the server and a set of tools. Run it with no command to start the server. Every command takes --help and prints the text this page is written from.
- [Zurg Tags Documentation](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/reference/tags.md): This document describes all possible tags that can be automatically applied to torrents in Zurg.
- [The MCP endpoint](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/reference/mcp.md): zurg can answer an AI agent over the Model Context Protocol: the client asks what tools exist, zurg describes them, and the agent calls them to read the library, work out why a release is not playing, repair it, or drive the media servers.
- [Outbound request identity](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/reference/outbound-identity.md): user_agent controls the shared HTTP User-Agent for debrid APIs and CDN reads, Newznab searches, NZB downloads, OpenSubtitles, ffprobe probes, media-server integrations, dependency downloads, updates and optional sharing/log exports.
- [Changelog](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/reference/changelog.md): TorBox has a flag that makes an add refuse anything it does not already hold. It is in their API but in none of their documentation, and zurg was not using it: a cached-only grab added the torrent, waited to see whether it completed, and deleted it again when it turned out to be a real download.

## Internals

- [Architecture](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/internals/architecture.md): A map of what zurg is, how the pieces fit, and why each package exists. Aimed at someone about to change the code: it names the load-bearing decisions and the invariants that are easy to break without noticing.
- [Persistent read caches](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/internals/persistent-caches.md): Imported NZBs, Real-Debrid, AllDebrid and TorBox entries all retain their library state in data/*.zurgtorrent. These files describe the library. Read
- [The debrid baseline](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/internals/debrid-baseline.md): What zurg costs and how fast it feels on the debrid path — Real-Debrid, AllDebrid and TorBox. There is no competitor here. The contender is a later zurg, and this file is what it has to beat.
- [Torrent lifecycle on Real-Debrid AllDebrid and TorBox](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/internals/torrent-lifecycle.md): Measured on 2026-08-30 against live accounts. Everything below marked observed came out of a capture. Everything marked inferred did not and says why.
- [qBittorrent Web API contract as consumed by Sonarr and Radarr (develop)](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/internals/qbittorrent-client-contract.md): Source of truth: files fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com/{Sonarr/Sonarr,Radarr/Radarr}/develop/... and from qbittorrent/qBittorrent/master on 2026-08-27.
- [zurg naming](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/internals/naming.md): Almost every name zurg shows is computed, never stored. A release's folder name, a file's name inside it, and the on-disk filename of its cache record are all derived from the torrent on every lookup.
- [SABnzbd API contract as consumed by Sonarr and Radarr (develop)](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/internals/sabnzbd-client-contract.md): Source of truth: files fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com/{Sonarr/Sonarr,Radarr/Radarr}/develop/... on 2026-08-22. Every line number below was read out of those files.
- [Aligning the Plex trash sweep with zurg's own file status](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/internals/plex-trash-sweep.md): The Plex trash sweep currently decides what to remove from a Plex library using file absence plus an age timer. zurg already knows something far better — whether the content behind that file is repairable or permanently dead — and does not consult it.
- [Proxied stream timeout regression](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/internals/stream-timeout-regression.md): Zurg used download_timeout_secs as a wall-clock deadline for proxied HTTP downloads. Its default is 15 seconds, so any single upstream response whose body took longer than 15 seconds to finish was cut off even while bytes were arriving normally.
- [Empty imports after a refused move](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/internals/rclone-move-refusal.md): Reproduced with rclone 1.72.0, a local-first union, VFS full caching and the .NET 6 File.Move(source, destination) used by Sonarr 4.0.19.2979.
- [Directory Configuration UI/UX Assessment](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/internals/uiux.md): Page: Directory Configuration at http://localhost:9999/directories/.
- [E2E Testing](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/internals/e2e-test.md): End-to-end tests to verify zurg is working correctly after deployment.
- [Torrents](https://notes.debridmediamanager.com/internals/realdebrid-behavior.md): Real-debrid supports downloading unlimited number of torrent files and magnet links, also selecting which files in it that you want to download If the
